assump.title: Assumptions and limits
assump.dataText: Script v{{v}} of {{date}}; frame {{frame}}; light-time correction “{{ab}}”; {{step}}-min step.
assump.optionsText: {{days}}-day stay; Sun's edge counted: {{limb}}; score = {{e}}% energy + {{c}}% communication.
limits: The Sun is treated as a point unless the edge option is on.
Terrain is known at 80 m; small rocks and the lander mast are not modelled.
Real power depends on solar panel orientation, which this tool does not simulate.
Some site coordinates are approximate and must be verified.

help.title: Help, method and sources
help.lead: How the figures are computed and where the data comes from.

methodItems.h: 1. Where are the Sun and Earth?
methodItems.p: NASA JPL ephemerides give their positions hour by hour as seen from each site, with the light-travel-time correction.
From the LOLA elevation model we compute, for 720 directions, the highest terrain angle within 150 km: the horizon mask.
A body is visible when its height exceeds the mask height in its direction.
We count sunlit hours, the longest night and the windows when Earth is visible, then combine them into a weighted score.
